pencereler.0-5: At cruising altitude, a jet's engine suddenly blew apart. Debris shattered a window, and
pencereler.5-12: one passenger was killed. The cause was a single fan blade. A fatigue crack had grown inside it. When
pencereler.12-20: it snapped, the engine's inlet broke up. Fragments struck the fuselage and the window gave way. The captain still landed the jet
pencereler.20-30: safely in Philadelphia. Fan blades were then checked more often with ultrasound.

segmentler.metin: Southwest Airlines Flight 1380 had an engine fail and a window break in flight.
It took only a fatigue crack in one fan blade.
So how could a fatigue crack in one fan blade do this?
The answer is fan blade fatigue fracture causing an uncontained engine failure and inlet debris strike — and it is why fan blade inspections were accelerated with ultrasound checks.
